title: Blood Pressure Measurement (Palpate)
content_markdown:
#### Indications

- As part of a normal patient assessment.

#### Procedure

- Explain the procedure to the patient and ensure they are positioned at rest.

- Expose the patient’s arm.

- Select an appropriate sized blood pressure cuff (covering approx 2/3 upper arm).

- Apply the blood pressure cuff, ensuring that the “Artery Line” is positioned approximately over the brachial artery and that the cuff is above the elbow.

- Locate the patient’s radial pulse.

- Inflate the cuff slowly until the radial pulse can no longer be palpated.

- Slowly release the pressure and record the reading at which the radial pulse returns.

#### Contraindications

- Mastectomies. Do not take a BP on the arm same side as the surgery (lymphoedema).

#### Complications

- Taking a BP over clothing or on a patient that is moving around may cause an inaccurate reading.

#### Specific Notes

- A radial pulse may not be palpable when the blood pressure is below approximately 80-90mm/Hg. A femoral pulse indicates a blood pressure of approx 70-80. A carotid only pulse is indicative of a blood pressure of 60-70.
- Avoid taking a BP on a dialysis patient on the same arm as the fistula, unless absolutely necessary. This also applies to a patient with a cannula in-situ.
